xep.header:
MUX Voice Channels This specification adds voice channels to Multi-User eXchange rooms: standing calls on a conference server outside XMPP that the MUX service admits members to by a URL and a token, whose participants it publishes on a pubsub node, and whose moderation it fronts. The media protocol is out of scope. &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council
XMPP Core XEP-0004 XEP-0030 XEP-0059 XEP-0060 XEP-0082 XEP-0128 XEP-0421 XEP-0482 XEP-xxxx
mux-chat-voice
Paavel A. pd@narayana.im pd@narayana.im
0.0.1 2026-11-23 pa
First draft.

section1.p: A voice channel is a standing call that members of a MUX room drop into: everyone who may see the channel sees who is in it without joining the media, and moderators mute, deafen, move and disconnect there. The MUX service has no media server of its own. A voice channel is one room on a conference server that the client reaches by a URL and a token; the service is the token authority, the occupancy publisher and the moderation front. What the client and the conference server say to each other is not defined here: a service names the transport in discovery, and a client that does not speak it shows the channel as one it cannot enter.

This document extends the Multi-User eXchange framework (XEP-xxxx, shortname mux-chat, called "the framework" below) with the channel kind voice, its form, its options at creation, three IQs and one pubsub node in the namespace urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0. The permissions it uses - connect, speak, video, share-screen, mute-members, move-members, request-to-speak - are in the framework's catalogue and evaluated by its algorithm.

ul.li: Who is in a call is visible to whoever may see the channel, without presence and after a reconnect.
The service admits by the room's permissions, and what it admits the conference server enforces.
Moderation is persistent: a server mute or a ban holds across leaving, rejoining and restarts.
The conference server never learns a JID.
The media protocol is replaceable.

section1.p: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in &rfc2119; and &rfc8174; when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

Terms not defined here (service, room, channel, member, guest, occupant id, hat, permission, the hierarchy) are the framework's. Statements without a keyword describe what the service does and are normative for it.

di.dd: The server that carries media, outside XMPP, reached by a URL.
What the conference server accepts for one connection: issued by the service, bound to the member's occupant id and to the grants its permissions give.
A member the conference server lists in the call; one item of the occupancy node.
A voice channel where only speakers publish and the audience raises hands.

section1.p: A voice channel is a channel of kind voice: listed in the room's channel node with <channel kind='voice'/>, never in disco#items of the service (which lists text channels for MUC clients). Its disco#info MUST carry the identity conference/audio-video, the features urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0, urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0, urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0 and urn:xmpp:spaces:0, the framework's two forms, and a form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0#info. It MUST NOT carry a conference/text identity or the http://jabber.org/protocol/muc feature, so a MUC client does not offer it as a chat; a MUC join presence is answered with <feature-not-implemented/> of type cancel whose text names this namespace.

example.caption: A voice channel's disco#info (the framework's forms left out)

section1.example: <iq type='result' from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='juliet@example.org/balcony' id='d1'> <query xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info'> <identity category='conference' type='audio-video' name='Verona · Lounge'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:spaces:0'/> <x xmlns='jabber:x:data' type='result'> <field var='FORM_TYPE' type='hidden'><value>urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0#info</value></field> <field var='voice#room' type='jid-single'><value>verona@mux.example.org</value></field> <field var='voice#transport'><value>livekit</value></field> <field var='voice#participants'><value>3</value></field> <field var='voice#max'><value>25</value></field> <field var='voice#video' type='boolean'><value>1</value></field> <field var='voice#screen' type='boolean'><value>1</value></field> <field var='voice#stage' type='boolean'><value>0</value></field> <field var='voice#e2ee'><value>none</value></field> </x> </query> </iq>

tr.td: the room the channel belongs to
the media protocol the conference server speaks, by a registered name (Transports); none while the service has no conference server, and a <join/> is then refused
how many are in the call now: the occupancy node's items
the most participants
voice#video, voice#screen
whether cameras and screen sharing are allowed
1: a stage channel

the media encryption: none in this version, meaning the conference server's operator can hear the call; other values are defined by the documents that define a key exchange, together with the requires entry that gates the channel

section1.p: The conference server's URL is not in discovery; it comes with the token.

At creation and update a voice channel takes, in the framework's #channelconfig form, the fields voice-max (1 to 250, default 25), voice-video, voice-screen, voice-stage (booleans, default 1, 1, 0) and voice-e2ee (none); on a channel of another kind they are <bad-request/>. A changed option applies to tokens issued from then on, and the service brings the participants in the call into line.

A member joins the call by an empty <join/> to the channel JID. The result gives the conference server's url, a token for one connection, the member's identity there (its occupant id in the room, the same its messages carry), the conference server's room name (informative), when the token expires for a new connection, and the e2ee in force. The client connects to url with token by the transport named in discovery.
section1.example:
<iq type='set' to='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' id='j1'> <join xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0'/> </iq>
<iq type='result' from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='juliet@example.org/balcony' id='j1'> <join xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0' url='wss://sfu.example.org' token='eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJkZDcyNjAzZCJ9.5Qx3n2vY8sK1pL7aR4eT9uW0zC6bN3mF' identity='dd72603dXh3o6qK2pL9sW1Yz' room='3vU3sYqgX0h3f1yGJm1qH0U3rI7Vb1Hj0N3C0f6dQ5E' expires='2026-11-23T12:10:00Z' e2ee='none'/> </iq>
section1.p: The service MUST check, in this order, and answer the first failure:

ol.li: the channel is a live voice channel the requester may see, else <item-not-found/>, as discovery says;
the session may use the channel (the framework's requirements gate), else <not-acceptable/> with <requires/>;
the requester is a member of the room, else <forbidden/> with <not-member/>;
it is not voice-banned in the channel, else <forbidden/> with <banned/>, whose until names the ban's end when it has one;
the call is not full: the participants and the tokens issued lately that have not connected, the requester not counted, are fewer than voice#max, else <not-allowed/> with <channel-full/>;
the requester is under the service's rate of joins, else <resource-constraint/> of type wait;
the conference server is configured and answers, else <service-unavailable/> of type wait with <sfu-down/>.

section1.p: The application conditions are in this namespace. A requester that is no member of the room MAY ask to join as a guest by putting the framework's <guest/> (and a <nick/>) in the <join/>: it is admitted to the room as the framework's guest join would admit it, refused as that would refuse it, and then checked as above. The token's grants follow the permissions, not the request: publishing a microphone needs speak, a camera video and voice#video, a screen share-screen and voice#screen; a server mute takes a source away and a server deafening takes subscribing away.

One call per room. A member in another voice channel of the same room is removed from it when it joins this one. One connection per member. The identity is the occupant id, so a second device of one member replaces the first; the occupancy node counts members, not devices.

To leave, the client disconnects from the conference server and then, as a courtesy, sends an empty <leave/> to the channel JID, answered with an empty result. The service verifies with the conference server before it retracts the item; it MUST NOT remove a participant on a <leave/> alone, so a late leave from a replaced device does not cut the device that replaced it. A crashed client is caught by the conference server and by the service's reconciliation.
The channel JID serves a &xep0060; node urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0#participants, published only by the service, with one item per participant whose id is the occupant id.
section1.example: <message from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='romeo@example.org' type='headline'> <event xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/pubsub#event'> <items node='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0#participants'> <item id='dd72603dXh3o6qK2pL9sW1Yz'> <participant xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0' nick='Juliet' since='2026-11-23T12:00:03Z'> <occupant-id xmlns='urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0' id='dd72603dXh3o6qK2pL9sW1Yz'/> <self-mute/> <server-mute media='camera' by='a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2'/> <camera/> <hand since='2026-11-23T12:04:00Z'/> </participant> </item> </items> </event> </message>

the room; the conference server
the identity, as &xep0421; writes it
the service

the participant is a guest
the service
<self-mute/>, <self-deaf/>
what the client said of itself
the client; not enforced
a moderator muted it; media absent for the microphone, else camera or screen; by the moderator's occupant id
the service; enforced

the service; enforced

section1.p: A participant leaving is a retraction of its item. An item MUST NOT carry a real JID. Speaking activity is not published; it is the call's own.

Whoever may see the channel retrieves the items, paged by &xep0059;. Every member who sees the channel is subscribed by being a member; anyone else who sees it MAY subscribe. Notifications are type='headline' messages to bare JIDs. The node's configuration is readable and never written: pubsub#type is this namespace, pubsub#access_model open when everyone sees the channel and whitelist otherwise, pubsub#publish_model publishers, pubsub#notify_retract, pubsub#deliver_payloads and pubsub#persist_items set, pubsub#max_items equal to voice#max, pubsub#notification_type headline, pubsub#send_last_published_item never. Clients never publish or retract (<forbidden/> with <publisher-not-allowed/>).
The subscription gate. A client MUST play only media whose identity is an item of the node. A participant the service did not announce is never heard.

section2.p: A participant reports its own flags by <state/> to the channel JID, the whole state each time; an absent child is off. The service answers with an empty result and mirrors the state in the item. It is accepted from a member with an item or a fresh token (else <not-allowed/> with <not-in-call/>); a state sent before the conference server lists the participant is kept for its item. <hand/> is accepted only on a stage channel from a holder of request-to-speak (else <not-allowed/>); a speaker's hand is dropped. The service MUST bound the rate (<policy-violation/> of type wait). The state is the client's word: a self-mute is the client's own track mute, and only server mutes are enforced.

example.caption: Juliet mutes herself and raises a hand

section2.example:
<iq type='set' to='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' id='s1'> <state xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0'><self-mute/><hand/></state> </iq>
<iq type='result' from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='juliet@example.org/balcony' id='s1'/>

section2.p: On a channel with voice#stage set only speakers publish. A member holding mute-members there is always a speaker; others become one by a moderator's <speaker/> and stop by <speaker value='0'/> or by leaving the call. The audience's tokens carry no publishing grant; <hand/> asks a moderator.

section1.p: A moderator acts on a participant by <moderate occupant-id='…'/> to the channel JID with exactly one action child.
section1.example:
<iq type='set' to='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' id='m1'> <moderate xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0' occupant-id='9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4'> <server-mute/> </moderate> </iq>
<iq type='result' from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='romeo@example.org/orchard' id='m1'/>

tr.td: <server-mute/>; media='camera' or 'screen' for that source; value='0' lifts
the source is taken out of the participant's grants and its tracks of that source muted; kept until lifted. Lifting gives the source back; the participant unmutes itself
<server-deaf/>; value='0' lifts
subscribing is taken away; kept until lifted
removed from the call, the item retracted; it may join again
<ban/>, optional until (&xep0082;, in the future); value='0' lifts
mute-members and move-members
removed, and refused at <join/> while the ban holds
move-members here and in the target

to is a live voice channel of the same room the member may connect to (else <bad-request/>); removed here, and told where to go by a headline message carrying <moved to='JID' by='occupant-id'/>; the client joins there
<speaker/>; value='0' sends back to the audience
stage channels only (else <bad-request/>); the hand dropped

example.caption: Tybalt is moved to the garden

section1.example: <message from='verona.lounge@mux.example.org' to='tybalt@example.org' type='headline'> <moved xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0' to='verona.garden@mux.example.org' by='a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2'/> </message>

ul.li: occupant-id names a member of the room (else <item-not-found/>); one's own is <not-allowed/>; a member the actor does not outrank, by the framework's hierarchy, is <forbidden/>.
<disconnect/>, <move/> and <speaker/> need the member in the call (else <item-not-found/> with <not-in-call/>); mutes, deafening and bans apply ahead of a join too.
A missing or unknown action, a bad media, value or until is <bad-request/>.

The result comes once the conference server has applied the change; when it does not answer, the reply is <service-unavailable/> with <sfu-down/>, and what the service keeps (a mute, a ban) stays and MUST be enforced at the next reconciliation.
Every enforced change is mirrored in the item.

section1.p: A server mute (per source), a server deafening and a voice ban MUST be kept per occupant id and channel and survive leaving, rejoining and restarts: the next token already lacks the source. Stage speakers are not kept; they are the call's state.

A "come to voice" is a &xep0482; invitation with a child of this namespace naming the channel. In a text channel it passes as any groupchat message and does not ring; as a direct message it is a personal call invitation and the answers are XEP-0482's. The receiving client SHOULD check by disco#info that channel is a voice channel before it offers to join.
section1.example: <message to='verona@mux.example.org' type='groupchat' id='inv1'> <invite xmlns='urn:xmpp:call-invites:0'> <voice xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0' channel='verona.lounge@mux.example.org'/> </invite> <body>Come to the Lounge</body> </message>

tr.td: no such channel, or one the requester may not see; a member not in the call (with <not-in-call/>) or not of the room, on a moderation
the session lacks what the channel requires, with the framework's <requires/>
not a member (with <not-member/>); no connect; voice-banned (with <banned/>); the hierarchy refusing a moderation
the call is full (with <channel-full/>); a state from a member not in the call (with <not-in-call/>); a hand without request-to-speak or off a stage; a moderation of oneself
a voice option on a channel of another kind or out of range; a bad action, media, value, until or to; a stage action off a stage
states or leaves sent faster than the service allows
joins faster than the service allows
the conference server is not configured or does not answer (with <sfu-down/>)
a MUC join presence to a voice channel

ul.li: The service MUST reconcile its view with the conference server: while a call is live it asks the server who is in, after a join, after a leave and after each moderation, and publishes an item for each participant that is a member of the room holding connect there and not voice-banned; removes from the server a participant that is none of that, including an identity that names no member; brings each participant's grants into line with what its token would say now; and retracts the items of participants the server no longer lists. A destroyed channel or room has its conference room deleted.

Exactly one authority talks to the conference server for a channel at a time; when that authority changes (a failover), media keep flowing and the new one rebuilds the occupancy node from the server's answer.
A client MUST treat voice#e2ee none as a call the conference server's operator can hear and MUST say so in its user interface.
A voice channel has no text side; no "joined the call" lines are written to a text channel.
A service with no conference server configured answers voice#transport none, keeps the channel listed and refuses joins, so a client shows the channel as unavailable rather than missing.

section1.p: The reference implementation uses the namespace https://ns.another.im/mux/voice/0 in place of urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0, the node and the form type under it, until this document is accepted; the two are the same wire.

With the livekit transport the conference room's name is a hash of the namespace, the service's domain and the channel's internal id, so a renamed channel keeps its call and the server sees no JID; tokens are valid for ten minutes for a new connection; reconciliation asks the server every 20 seconds while a call is live.

Media encryption is left to a later version: the intended design carries each participant's frame key as an application message of the channel's end-to-end encrypted group, and a client that cannot encrypt frames is then refused rather than joined in clear.

ul.li: The service holds the conference server's credentials; clients receive a token for one connection with the least grants and never call the server's administrative interface. The token is a bearer secret: it MUST be carried only over an encrypted stream and SHOULD NOT be logged; a service MUST give it a short life for a new connection, so that a token at rest in a client's memory is worth little.

Because the identity is the occupant id, a second connection with a valid token replaces the first: a token that leaks within its life lets its holder displace the member's own device for as long as the member does not reconnect. The short life and the rate of joins bound this.
The conference server sees occupant ids, nicks, timing, packet sizes and audio levels; never JIDs or channel names.
A participant's own flags are its word; enforcement is the server's grants, set by the service.

Reconciliation removes every participant the room does not admit, so a leaked token stops working within one reconciliation interval of its holder losing standing, and the subscription gate keeps an unannounced participant silent meanwhile. A client that does not apply the gate may play media from a participant the room never admitted.

Guests join calls by the framework's rules and hold the guest hat's voice permissions only; a room that does not want guests in its calls closes the channel to the guest hat by an overwrite or sets guests to 0.
Joins, states and leaves are rate-limited per member and channel; a service MUST refuse beyond its bounds rather than relay them to the conference server.
Moderation actions are audited by the service as any other, naming the target by occupant id and nick.

Who is in a call, since when, and with what flags is published to everyone who may see the channel, member or not in the call; that is the point of the occupancy node, and a member who does not want it joins no call.

The conference server is a third party to XMPP: it learns the occupant ids and nicks of the participants and the media metadata of a call, and, while voice#e2ee is none, the media themselves. Its operator may differ from the service's.
The service learns when each member joins and leaves a call; nothing of the media.

section1.p: This document requires no interaction with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).

section2.p: This specification defines the XML namespace urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0. Upon advancement of this specification from a status of Experimental to a status of Draft, the ®ISTRAR; shall add it to the registry located at &NAMESPACES;, as described in Section 4 of &xep0053;. If the namespace is modified in a way that is not backwards-compatible, its version number shall be incremented from "0" to "1" (and so on).

section2.code: <var> <name>urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0</name> <desc>The entity is a MUX voice channel.</desc> <doc>XEP-xxxx</doc> </var>

section2.p: This specification defines the channel kind voice of the framework's kind field.
&xep0068; defines a process for standardizing the fields used within Data Forms. The Registrar shall include the following form and fields in its registry (see &FORMTYPES;):
section2.code:
<form_type> <name>urn:xmpp:mux-chat:voice:0#info</name> <doc>XEP-xxxx</doc> <desc>A voice channel, in its disco#info.</desc> <field var='voice#room' type='jid-single' label='The room'/> <field var='voice#transport' type='text-single' label='The media transport'/> <field var='voice#participants' type='text-single' label='Participants now'/> <field var='voice#max' type='text-single' label='Most participants'/> <field var='voice#video' type='boolean' label='Cameras allowed'/> <field var='voice#screen' type='boolean' label='Screen sharing allowed'/> <field var='voice#stage' type='boolean' label='Stage channel'/> <field var='voice#e2ee' type='text-single' label='Media encryption'/> </form_type>
<form_type> <name>urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#channelconfig</name> <doc>XEP-xxxx</doc> <field var='voice-max' type='text-single' label='Most participants'/> <field var='voice-video' type='boolean' label='Cameras allowed'/> <field var='voice-screen' type='boolean' label='Screen sharing allowed'/> <field var='voice-stage' type='boolean' label='Stage channel'/> <field var='voice-e2ee' type='text-single' label='Media encryption'/> </form_type>

section2.p: The Registrar shall maintain a registry of values of the voice#transport field. Each entry names the protocol a client speaks to the conference server, what the url of a <join/> result is, and what the token is. The registration template:
section2.code: <transport> <name>the value of voice#transport</name> <desc>the client protocol, the meaning of url and the form of token</desc> <doc>the document that defines them</doc> </transport>

<transport> <name>none</name> <desc>No conference server is configured; a join is refused.</desc> <doc>XEP-xxxx</doc> </transport> <transport> <name>livekit</name> <desc>The conference server speaks the LiveKit client protocol (https://docs.livekit.io/). url is the signalling WebSocket URL; token is a LiveKit access token whose identity is the member's occupant id, whose display name is the member's nick and whose grants are exactly those the Joining section derives from the member's permissions: room join, subscribing unless server-deafened, and the publishable sources (microphone, camera, screen share) it may use; no administrative, recording, room-creation or listing grant, no hidden participation and no metadata updates. The conference room name is opaque to the client.</desc> <doc>XEP-xxxx</doc> </transport>

section1.p: The occupancy node and the token-authority role follow what MatrixRTC does with a conference server; the stage mode and the sticky server mute follow what users of voice channels elsewhere expect.
